question: Will Sinokor keep sailing Hormuz, yes or no?

lines.text: Iran has blacklisted Sinokor, whose tankers carried thirty seven percent of Hormuz oil last month.
Its new strait authority says every Sinokor ship will face legal action from the first of November.
It says Sinokor committed the most violations in three months.

scene.quote: committed the highest number of passage violations over the past three months
scene.who: Persian Gulf Strait Authority, on X

lines.text: And it says action has already been taken against at least seven of its ships.
Maritime Executive says those seven were attacked in the strait.
Sinokor is South Korean. Bloomberg calls it the world's biggest tanker owner.
It moved over one hundred and five million barrels through Hormuz in September, Bloomberg says.
Lloyd's List estimates half of all tankers crossing are now linked to Sinokor.
Iran's navy also says a tanker hit mines east of the strait and caught fire.
It says the tanker had switched off its tracking.
Sinokor has not commented. The US has sanctioned Iran's strait authority.
Iran says it controls who crosses. Washington says the lanes are open.
Day two hundred and forty three tomorrow. Will Sinokor keep sailing Hormuz, yes or no?
